The word 'brother' is printed in black lowercase script on the front of the machine body in both photos.
A small screen on the right side shows a colorful icon/image, but the resolution is too low to read any model text or menu details.
No power cord, foot pedal, embroidery arm/hoop, spool caps, or accessory case is visible in either photo.
No photo shows the machine powered on, a stitch sample, or a close-up of the nameplate/model sticker usually found on the back or base.
A watermark 'ABIOLAONIMACHINE' and 'POSTED ON JIJI' overlays both images, consistent with a resale listing screenshot.

No nameplate, sticker, or screen text showing 'SE630' is legible in either photo

claims.claim: Computerized Sewing and Embroidery Machine (functional claim implied)
claims.evidence: No power-on shot, stitch sample, or screen menu visible to confirm working electronics

risks.risk: Model cannot be confirmed, and price for Brother sewing/embroidery machines varies greatly by model (entry-level vs SE630-class).
risks.proof: Clear close-up photo of the nameplate/model sticker on the back or base of the machine, or a screen photo showing the model name on the LCD startup screen
risks.if_unproven: priced as a generic unidentified Brother sewing machine, lowest tier for that type

risks.risk: Machine may not power on or may have faulty motor/electronics
risks.proof: Short video clip of the machine powered on, needle moving, and a stitch being sewn on fabric

risks.risk: Embroidery unit, foot pedal, power cord, and hoops may be missing, which are essential for an embroidery-capable machine
risks.proof: Photo of all included accessories laid out together (pedal, cord, embroidery arm, hoops, bobbins)
risks.if_unproven: priced as bare machine only, without embroidery accessories

risks.risk: Authenticity of branding cannot be confirmed from a logo alone; could be a counterfeit or rebadged unit
risks.proof: Photo of the serial number plate alongside a matching Brother authenticity check or official packaging/manual
risks.if_unproven: priced as unverified brand authenticity, worst case as generic machine

risks.risk: Cosmetic or mechanical damage (cracked casing, bent needle plate, worn belt) may be hidden by the bedding and angle
risks.proof: Close-up photos of all sides of the machine, including underside and needle area
risks.if_unproven: priced as possibly damaged, worst case condition

proof_requests: Clear close-up photo of the model/nameplate sticker (usually on the back or base of the machine)
Video of the machine powered on, threading and stitching a sample on fabric
Photo of all included accessories: foot pedal, power cord, embroidery arm, hoops, bobbins, manual
Close-up photos of the machine body from multiple angles to check for cracks or damage
response.reason: The brand Brother is visible, but the specific model (SE630) that determines the price tier cannot be read from either photo, and no proof of working condition or included accessories is shown.
